exposure: Transumbilical laparoendoscopic single-site surgery (TU-LESS) for gynecological diseases during pregnancy
outcome: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. Cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 75 pregnant women who underwent TU-LESS for gynecological diseases (adnexal mass, adnexal torsion, ruptured adnexal mass, intrauterine pregnancy combined with ectopic pregnancy) between September 2019 and May 2024 at West China Second Hospital, Sichuan University.
finding: TU-LESS is a safe and effective method for treating gynecological diseases during the first and second trimesters of pregnancy, with few perioperative complications, and the umbilical incision sutured with Zheng's anchor suturing technique can withstand the tension of a growing abdomen and labor.
mod_finding: Among 56 patients with live births, 27 had vaginal delivery and 29 had Cesarean section, and no incisional dehiscence or hernia occurred in patients who underwent vaginal delivery.
followup_time: The interval from TU-LESS to childbirth was 23.3 ± 4.4 weeks for those who had live births; specific duration of follow-up for cosmetic satisfaction and incisional complications is not explicitly stated beyond childbirth.
gest_age: The study included patients in their first and second trimesters of pregnancy.
